text:
Per-query candidate-set z-scoring preserves each component’s ranking but can change their blended ranking. Algebraically, for SASRec score s and transition score t, the fused pairwise difference is αΔs/σs(C)+(1−α)Δt/σt(C): means cancel, while candidate-dependent standard deviations change the effective weights. Thus sampled candidates, the full catalog, and individual inference chunks can reverse the order of the same two items. Sparse transition probabilities make this especially sensitive to candidate composition. This is a mathematical consequence of the normalization formula, not a measured RecHarness result.

Fixed training-derived scaling makes each item’s fused score independent of other candidates: estimate component scales separately per category using a reproducible training-only reference distribution, freeze them with an epsilon floor, and tune the blend on validation. Keep the transition probability denominator fixed as well. This preserves pairwise ordering across sampled and full-catalog scoring, though HR@10 naturally changes with competitors. Rank fusion avoids score calibration, but candidate-local ranks remain set-dependent. [Reciprocal rank fusion](https://plg.uwaterloo.ca/~gvcormac/cormacksigir09-rrf.pdf) uses Σ1/(k+rank); consistency requires computing full-catalog component ranks and then restricting to evaluation candidates.

Exact per-query global normalization also works: first stream the entire declared catalog universe to accumulate each component’s mean and variance; then rescore chunks using those shared statistics and merge top-k. [Mergeable Welford statistics](https://max.modular.com/stable/api/mojo/algorithm/reduce_op/Welford/) support this without storing all scores. Use the identical normalization universe for sampled evaluation and recommendations, apply eligibility masks consistently, and break ties deterministically. Chunk-local normalization is inconsistent; global normalization is chunk-invariant up to floating-point rounding. Frozen training-derived scales are the simplest reproducible default; global normalization retains query-adaptive scaling at additional computation cost.
